content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge labels Matthew 1:20 UNDERDETERMINED by setting the challenger's covenant-presence sense against the defender's physical-source sense, which is the two-sense situation the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — I weighed (1) Matthew 1:20 carries both covenant-presence and physical-source senses, so UNDERDETERMINED is forbidden, and (2) the two answers merely address separate aspects not competing senses, which would not trigger the rule.", "why": "Because the rule forbids treating a verse with two simultaneous senses as open and requires both senses to stand, using those two senses as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED breaches K-S2."}
